chapter: War years, Goodman and Woody Herman
title: Postwar: a USO band that never flew, then Woody Herman
summary: A planned troop-entertainment band with Flip Phillips and Ralph Burns never got off the ground, so Norvo joined Woody Herman at the Paramount for about a year.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: And fellas like Shorty were coming out of the Service and Gazzo Gazzo was coming out of the Service, he'd been with the Artie Shaw band --
-- other guys were coming -- they'd call me.

So, Benny was set on these guys, so Woody wanted Shorty and he also wanted Gazzo. And I'd had a band for a short while with Flip Phillips and Ralph Burns, Dick Taylor Johnny Blowers, Clyde Lombardi, we were going for Coca-Cola to England to entertain the troops, but it never got off the ground. For about six months, we were around New York and we made some V discs with them, too --
We got paid, but the USO wouldn't let us get off the ground, that's when the USO was formed.
So I had a kinmanship with the band from both Flip and Ralph Burns --
-- so I guess it was just a natural thing that I went with Woody, because he had been wanting me to come with the band --
-- and so finally I said, 'All right, fine.' So I joined him at the Paramount.
And that lasted about a year.
